_comment: EDITABLE spec consumed by make_manifest.py. Each segment is [start_s, end_s] into the beat's source capture, or [start_s, end_s, 'other-file.mp4'] to pull that segment from a different raw take. Durations in manifest.json are MEASURED with ffprobe, never copied from here.

corpus.window: 11:00-11:09 local, pinned by WHODUNIT_WINDOW_END_MS/_H so the differential verify sees this corpus and nothing later

beats.title: The citation - SigNoz/signoz#1957, still open
beats.narration: SigNoz's co-founder asked for this in January 2023. It is still open. This is the implementation - and instead of a side-by-side panel, it hands you the query.
beats.notes: Title, #1957, Open badge, pranay01, Jan 2 2023 all legible before the scroll. Recorded headless with Playwright.

beats.title: One scan, THE ELIMINATION BOARD
beats.narration: One question to ClickHouse. Then the whole itemset lattice is enumerated locally. The machine considers the obvious answers - the edge alone, the missing flag-service alone - and rejects them. Only the conjunction separates the cohorts.
beats.notes: One real 472.3s run; the spinner plays that wait back in 5s with its counter ramping to the true elapsed, which is then printed.

beats.title: The flat baseline fails on the same cohort
beats.narration: This is what every flat tool sees - BubbleUp, compare, Trace Patterns. Its best single predicate lands at precision 0.17. The fault needs two conditions at once, and no single predicate can see it.
beats.notes: benchmark/baseline.py on the identical matrix. Top pick NOT edge__shop_checkout__GET_flags_evaluate, precision 0.17, recall 1.00 - fails the 0.80/0.50 gate.

beats.title: Compiled query + verification receipt
beats.narration: No model wrote this. It is compiled into SigNoz's own trace-operator grammar, then run back against the live engine. Whodunit mined 61 traces; SigNoz returned 61. They agree.
beats.notes: Leaves A/B/C, (A => B) && NOT C, returnSpansFrom A, then the differential receipt and the verdict hash.

beats.title: The permalink, opened in SigNoz Trace Explorer
beats.narration: That permalink opens the machine-written query in SigNoz's own Explorer. Same language, same engine - three leaves, the operator, the matched set. Open one trace and the shape is right there: payment retries redis, and flag-service never ran.
beats.notes: compositeQuery is double-URL-encoded and carries builder.queryTraceOperator (materialize/NOTES.md 1). The Explorer renders all three leaves and the operator, and the flame graph shows redis-retry under shop-payment with no shop-flag-service span.

beats.title: Arm it - and it fires
beats.narration: One flag arms it. The discriminator becomes a native SigNoz alert with warning and critical thresholds. Replay the fault and the webhook fires - the rule id in that POST is the rule the command just created. Everyone else stops at a panel.
beats.notes: Armed live (rule 019f97fb-f4a7-743a-8499-be519fb5bbeb); the middle segment is SigNoz's own Alert Rules page showing the rule plotted against both threshold lines. The ~1-3 min evaluation delay is cut out of one continuous take.

beats.title: Determinism - two live runs, one hash
beats.narration: Same input, same seed, same hash - every time. No LLM anywhere in the runtime. This is deterministic.
beats.notes: Two complete live runs (scan, mine the whole lattice, compile, verify). The mining waits are played back compressed; the hashes are not touched.

beats.title: The repo and the one command that reproduces it
beats.narration: Everyone shows you the difference. Only SigNoz can arm it. One command reproduces the whole thing.
beats.notes: foundryctl cast is typed but deliberately not run - the live stack already owns :8080 / :4318. casting.yaml.lock is committed next to it.
